newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore opposition leaders found in contempt.
newsitem.headline: Singapore opposition leaders found in contempt.

text.p: A Singapore parliamentary committee said on Friday that four leaders of the main opposition party had acted in contempt of parliament and recommended that they be fined.

The committee of privileges recommended parliament fine Singapore Democratic Party (SDP) secretary-general Chee Soon Juan Singapore $25,000 (US$17,900) and that three other SDP leaders receive fines ranging from S$5,000 to S$13,000.

The punishment for contempt of parliament can be as high as S$50,000 and a jail term. Chee and the others could also be barred from contesting future elections if parliament passed on the case to a civil court which then found against them.
But if parliament follows the committee recommendations, that should leave the four free to run in the general election Singapore must hold by April, as Chee is widely expected to do.

The committee said Chee had fabricated data and falsified documents presented to a select committee, and subsequently misled it when challenged over the figures. The others were found in contempt in relation to the same committee hearings.
Chee said the figure was a typing mistake and a result of human error.
"I deny the allegation that I have presented false documents to the Select Committee with the intent to deceive," Chee told the committee of privileges.
